$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-4z &=-10 \\ y+z &=4 \\ z &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system."] [:db/add "1007a5f6-391d-5dfe-af79-afe606693838" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -4 & -10 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}-R_{3},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -4 & -10 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+4R_{3},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=6 \\ y &=0 \\ z &=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

So, we have the solution $x=6$, $y=0$, and $z=4$. $$

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+4R_{3},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].

$$

So, we have the solution $x=6$, $y=0$, and $z=4$. Or, in vector form, $\langle 6,0,4\rangle$.
